intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SLC5A1 gene (182380), which encodes the sodium/glucose cotransporter SGLT1, on chromosome 22q12.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SLC5A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of the amplified products has revealed a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract links an SGLT1 mutation to GGM in one family. It does not say the mutation was homozygous, and it does not mention compound heterozygosity.

checks.claim: The SLC5A1 gene encodes the sodium/glucose cotransporter SGLT1.
checks.evidence_quote: We have previously cloned and sequenced a Na+/glucose cotransporter from normal human ileum and shown that this gene, SGLT1, resides on the distal q arm of chromosome 22.
checks.explanation: SGLT1 is the Na+/glucose cotransporter. SLC5A1 is the approved gene symbol.

checks.claim: The SLC5A1 gene is located on chromosome 22q12.
checks.evidence_quote: caused by mutations in the Na(+) /glucose cotransporter gene SLC5A1
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene.

paragraphs.text: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is an autosomal recessive disorder of intestinal monosaccharide transport. It presents in the neonatal period with severe, watery, acidic diarrhea and dehydration that begin when the infant is fed breast milk or formula containing lactose, glucose, or galactose. Removing these sugars from the diet stops the diarrhea. Fructose is absorbed normally and can be used as the carbohydrate source. Some patients also have mild renal glucosuria.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is an autosomal recessive disease
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is a disorder of intestinal monosaccharide transport.
checks.evidence_quote: AN INBORN DEFECT OF INTESTINAL ABSORPTION OF CERTAIN MONOSACCHARIDES.
checks.explanation: Title describes an inborn defect of intestinal absorption of certain monosaccharides.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption presents in the neonatal period.
checks.evidence_quote: manifesting within the first weeks of life
checks.explanation: Onset in the first weeks of life is the neonatal period.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption presents with severe, watery, acidic diarrhea.
checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal
checks.explanation: The abstract says the diarrhea is severe but does not call it watery or acidic.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption presents with dehydration.
checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.
checks.explanation: Dehydration is stated.

checks.claim: In glucose/galactose malabsorption, diarrhea and dehydration begin when the infant is fed breast milk or formula containing lactose, glucose, or galactose.
checks.evidence_quote: selective failure to absorb dietary glucose and galactose from the intestine. The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration
checks.explanation: The abstract says the symptoms follow from dietary glucose and galactose. It does not mention breast milk, formula or lactose.

checks.claim: In glucose/galactose malabsorption, removing lactose, glucose, and galactose from the diet stops the diarrhea.
checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.
checks.explanation: The abstract implies that removing the sugars is life-saving. It does not say outright that this stops the diarrhea, and it does not mention lactose.

checks.claim: In glucose/galactose malabsorption, fructose is absorbed normally.
checks.evidence_quote: All subjects accumulated fructose similarly.
checks.explanation: Fructose uptake by jejunal mucosa in vitro was normal; normal absorption in the body is implied but not stated.

checks.claim: In glucose/galactose malabsorption, fructose can be used as the carbohydrate source.
checks.evidence_quote: All the children responded clinically to fructose-based formula, and they are thriving at follow-up.
checks.explanation: A fructose-based formula was used successfully in all eight children.

checks.claim: Some patients with glucose/galactose malabsorption have mild renal glucosuria.
checks.evidence_quote: A partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption was found in the proband.
checks.explanation: A partial renal reabsorption defect was found in one proband; glucosuria is not explicitly stated.

paragraphs.text: Lindquist and Meeuwisse (1962) and Laplane et al. (1962) first described the disorder. They reported infants who had life-threatening diarrhea from birth that resolved when glucose and galactose were removed from the diet.

checks.claim: Lindquist and Meeuwisse (1962) and Laplane et al. (1962) first described glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. Title only; earlier reports are not mentioned.

checks.claim: Lindquist and Meeuwisse (1962) and Laplane et al. (1962) reported infants with life-threatening diarrhea from birth.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. Title only.

checks.claim: In the infants reported by Lindquist and Meeuwisse (1962) and Laplane et al. (1962), the diarrhea resolved when glucose and galactose were removed from the diet.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. Title only.

paragraphs.text: Affected infants had watery diarrhea with acidic, sugar-containing stools, which led to severe dehydration and failure to thrive. Without treatment the disorder could be fatal. The diarrhea stopped when the infants were fed a fructose-based formula free of glucose and galactose. Mild intermittent glucosuria was reported, and some patients developed nephrocalcinosis or renal stones. With age, tolerance to glucose and galactose has been reported to improve somewhat.

checks.claim: Infants with glucose/galactose malabsorption had watery diarrhea.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinically, all affected individuals presented with classic watery diarrhea and dehydration.
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: Infants with glucose/galactose malabsorption had acidic stools.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. Title only.

checks.claim: Infants with glucose/galactose malabsorption had sugar-containing stools.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. Title only.

checks.claim: The diarrhea in glucose/galactose malabsorption led to severe dehydration.
checks.evidence_quote: The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal
checks.explanation: The abstract describes severe diarrhea and dehydration that can be fatal.

checks.claim: The diarrhea in glucose/galactose malabsorption led to failure to thrive.
checks.evidence_quote: They were first seen for chronic watery diarrhea, present since birth, and failure to thrive.
checks.explanation: Failure to thrive is reported alongside the diarrhea, but the abstract does not state that the diarrhea caused it.

checks.claim: Untreated glucose/galactose malabsorption could be fatal.
checks.evidence_quote: are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: The diarrhea of infants with glucose/galactose malabsorption stopped when they were fed a fructose-based formula free of glucose and galactose.
checks.evidence_quote: usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet
checks.explanation: The abstract says the sugars should be removed from the diet but does not mention a fructose-based formula.

checks.claim: Mild intermittent glucosuria was reported in glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: A partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption was found in the proband.
checks.explanation: A partial renal glucose reabsorption defect is reported, but 'mild intermittent glucosuria' is not explicitly described.

checks.claim: Some patients with glucose/galactose malabsorption developed nephrocalcinosis.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 11 cited papers. Title only.

checks.claim: Some patients with glucose/galactose malabsorption developed renal stones.
checks.evidence_quote: One child had a renal stone at the first visit, and another was discovered to have one on follow-up.
checks.explanation: Two of the eight children had renal stones.

checks.claim: In glucose/galactose malabsorption, tolerance to glucose and galactose has been reported to improve somewhat with age.
checks.evidence_quote: Familial glucose-galactose malabsorption: remission of glucose intolerance.
checks.explanation: The title reports remission of glucose intolerance. It does not mention galactose tolerance or age, and it gives no detail on how much tolerance improved.

paragraphs.text: GGM is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. This is shown by affected sibs born to unaffected parents, by parental consanguinity in many families, and by homozygous or compound heterozygous SLC5A1 mutations in affected individuals.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
checks.evidence_quote: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is an autosomal recessive disease
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Glucose/galactose malabsorption has occurred in affected sibs born to unaffected parents.
checks.evidence_quote: Previously we showed that two sisters with GGM had a missense mutation in the SGLT1 gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions two affected sisters but says nothing about whether their parents were affected.

checks.claim: Parental consanguinity is present in many families with glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: this large consanguineous family
checks.explanation: The abstract reports consanguinity in only one family, not in many families.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with glucose/galactose malabsorption carry homozygous or compound heterozygous SLC5A1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract reports one missense mutation in one family. It does not state zygosity or describe compound heterozygotes.

paragraphs.text: Turk et al. (1991) found a homozygous missense mutation in the SLC5A1 gene, asp28-to-asn (D28N), in 2 affected sisters with GGM. Their parents were heterozygous carriers. When expressed in Xenopus oocytes, the mutant protein did not transport sugar.

checks.claim: Turk et al. (1991) found a homozygous asp28-to-asn (D28N) missense mutation in the SLC5A1 gene in 2 affected sisters with glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of the amplified products has revealed a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a missense mutation that cosegregates with GGM. It does not name D28N, say the mutation was homozygous, or say the patients were 2 sisters; these details may be in the full text.

checks.claim: The parents of the 2 sisters with the SLC5A1 D28N mutation were heterozygous carriers.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state that the parents were heterozygous carriers; this may be in the full text.

checks.claim: When expressed in Xenopus oocytes, the SLC5A1 D28N mutant protein did not transport sugar.
checks.evidence_quote: results in a complete loss of Na(+)-dependent glucose transport in Xenopus oocytes injected with this complementary RNA
checks.explanation: Stated (the variant is not named in the abstract).

paragraphs.text: Martin et al. (1996) analyzed the SLC5A1 gene in a large series of patients with GGM. They found many different mutations, including missense, nonsense, frameshift, and splice site mutations. Expression studies in Xenopus oocytes showed that most of the missense mutations caused defective trafficking of the SGLT1 protein to the plasma membrane. Some mutant proteins did reach the membrane but did not transport sugar.

checks.claim: Martin et al. (1996) analyzed the SLC5A1 gene in a large series of patients with glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: The gene has now been screened in 30 new patients
checks.explanation: Screening 30 new patients fits the description of a large series.

checks.claim: Martin et al. (1996) found many different SLC5A1 mutations in glucose/galactose malabsorption patients, including missense, nonsense, frameshift, and splice site mutations.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not list the mutation types found. These details would be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Expression studies in Xenopus oocytes by Martin et al. (1996) showed that most SLC5A1 missense mutations caused defective trafficking of the SGLT1 protein to the plasma membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: Defects in Na+/glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) trafficking and function cause glucose-galactose malabsorption.
checks.explanation: The title and the mention of a heterologous expression system support trafficking defects, but the abstract does not name Xenopus oocytes or say that most missense mutations were affected.

checks.claim: Martin et al. (1996) found that some mutant SGLT1 proteins reached the plasma membrane but did not transport sugar.
checks.evidence_quote: Defects in Na+/glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) trafficking and function cause glucose-galactose malabsorption.
checks.explanation: The title implies some defects affect function rather than trafficking, but the abstract does not say outright that some mutant proteins reached the membrane yet did not transport sugar.

paragraphs.text: Treatment is lifelong dietary exclusion of glucose and galactose, including lactose and sucrose. Fructose serves as the main carbohydrate.

checks.claim: Treatment of glucose/galactose malabsorption is lifelong dietary exclusion of glucose and galactose, including lactose and sucrose.
checks.evidence_quote: usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet
checks.explanation: The abstract supports removing glucose and galactose from the diet. It does not say the exclusion is lifelong or mention lactose and sucrose.

checks.claim: In the treatment of glucose/galactose malabsorption, fructose serves as the main carbohydrate.
checks.evidence_quote: All the children responded clinically to fructose-based formula
checks.explanation: A fructose-based formula was used, but the abstract does not describe fructose as the main carbohydrate in long-term management.

paragraphs.text: Turk et al. (1991) found a homozygous asp28-to-asn (D28N) substitution in the SLC5A1 gene in 2 sisters with GGM. Their parents were heterozygous. When expressed in Xenopus oocytes, the mutant cotransporter did not transport sodium-dependent sugar.

checks.claim: Turk et al. (1991) found a homozygous asp28-to-asn (D28N) substitution in the SLC5A1 gene in 2 sisters with glucose/galactose malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequence analysis of the amplified products has revealed a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype
checks.explanation: The abstract does not name D28N, say the mutation was homozygous, or say the patients were 2 sisters; these details may be in the full text.

checks.claim: The parents of the 2 sisters with the SLC5A1 D28N substitution were heterozygous.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention the parents' heterozygosity; this may be in the full text.

checks.claim: When expressed in Xenopus oocytes, the SLC5A1 D28N mutant cotransporter did not transport sodium-dependent sugar.
checks.evidence_quote: results in a complete loss of Na(+)-dependent glucose transport in Xenopus oocytes injected with this complementary RNA
checks.explanation: Stated.
